description.narrative: The AACJ consortium in Burkina Faso will promote and facilitate a broad movement of impacted communities, IDPs and minorities (including women and youth) from multiple regions (Pathway 1). The programme will allow for existing groups, organizations and movements to join forces, to develop a shared narrative and to rally together on climate justice topics (Pathway 2). Varied civil society actors will be connected with the appropriate communication channels, delivering an inclusive and effective platform. The consortium will also address the reduction in civic space and limits to freedom of expression faced by climate movements, including women and youth groups, supporting official recognition of civil society structures and building capacity on mobilization. The programme will raise awareness of vulnerable and impacted groups – including indigenous people, women, youth, and IDPs – on environmental laws and climate policies and work with local communities to claim and defend their rights to a decent livelihood and healthy environment (Pathway 3). It will support local and indigenous communities to document, share and spread traditional knowledge and best practice AFRICANACTIVISTS FOR CLIMATE JUSTICE 69 regarding climate adaptation and resilience (Pathway 4) while ensuring this knowledge is acknowledged as a major resource for climate adaptation by policy makers. The AACJ consortium in Burkina Faso will advocate for public policies and practices for protecting the livelihoods of vulnerable groups, improving their resilience and promoting inclusive climate financing, and strengthen capacities of CSOs to participate in political processes

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermón is since 1997 a member of the international Oxfam confederation, sharing values and a strategic plan to achieve greater global impact. Intermón Oxfam fights, with and for disadvantaged populations and as part of a broad global movement, with the aim of eradicating injustice and poverty, and to ensure that all human beings can fully exercise their rights and enjoy a dignified life. Mission, Vision and Values are the components of Oxfam Intermón identity and guide its steps as an organisation and the ideal with which Oxfam Intermón wants to live in order to obtain a fairer world with greater solidarity.

comment.narrative: Burkina Faso have continued to lead a space for dialogue on climate justice created in 2022 on loss and damage. The third national conference on loss and damage, held on September 12 and 13, 2024 in Ouagadougou, brought together 45 participants from government, NGOs, farmers' organizations and civil society. To document and raise awareness of the impacts of climate change, a video story was produced and broadcast by the Confédération Paysanne du Faso (CPF). The story highlighted the effects of recurrentflooding on farmers and the losses they suffer. To strengthen the capacity for action of young activists and climate justice actors, training was provided in the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to create climate narratives. This action benefited 43 young activists, including 18 women. As a result, the capacities of climate movements and allies to use modern tools to influence climate policies were strengthened. In terms of influencing climate policies, Oxfam and its allies held a strategic meeting tostrengthen the involvement of civil society organizations (CSOs) in Burkina Faso's NDC process.

comment.narrative: Initially, Oxfam in Burkina Faso did not have targets under this indicator. However, with support from the Alliance Fund, a national mapping of climate activist organisations was conducted, culminating in a landmark national convening on 28 June 2025. During this event, more than 70 organisations and activists from all 13 regions of Burkina Faso adopted a National Charter, laying the groundwork for a coordinated and inclusive climate movement.
